purpose: Editorial research for original fictional Nigerian character voices. These notes are not a scraped conversation corpus, training dataset or claim of nationwide representativeness.

sources.title: Which Nigerian-Pidgin does Generative AI speak?
sources.finding: The authors identify meaningful differences between BBC-style and other written Naija genres in their evaluated data and models.
sources.designImplication: Do not use a news register as the sole model for intimate casual chat. This paper does not establish the quality of our current Haiku model.

sources.title: O, sha and abi as pragmatic markers in Nigerian English
sources.finding: Corpus analysis treats these particles as meaningful conversational markers with contextual functions.
sources.designImplication: Use particles for emphasis, softening or checking agreement, rather than scattering them randomly.

sources.title: The Multilingual Pragmatics of New Englishes
sources.finding: The study examines multilingual question tags and speakers' interpretations of Nigerian English usage.
sources.designImplication: Code-mixing is not evidence of low education. Character profession must not force a foreign voice or deny Pidgin competence.

sources.title: Naija Guru grammar guide
sources.finding: Provides a structured treatment of Nigerian Pidgin grammar.
sources.designImplication: Check recurring constructions against a language resource and native-speaker review; do not mechanically replace English words.

sources.title: Naija Guru dictionary
sources.finding: Provides searchable Nigerian Pidgin lexical entries.
sources.designImplication: Use as a lexical reference, not proof that a term is fashionable in October 2026 or fits every region.

sources.title: Nigerian slang of 2025
sources.finding: Connects several catchphrases with 2025 popular culture.
sources.designImplication: Older trend phrases need dated provenance. Do not label a 2025 trend newly coined in 2026.

sources.title: Nigerian slang words in 2026
sources.finding: Reports continued social-media use of several expressions including screenshot/evidence and admiration phrases.
sources.designImplication: Recent reporting supports contextual recognition, not compulsory use. Ganusi has varying framing across sources; avoid prescribing one universal meaning.

sources.title: Top Nigerian slang expressions
sources.finding: Discusses conversational reactions, composure, migration slang and expressions of coping.
sources.designImplication: Useful for interpretation; the headline's universal wording is not evidence every Nigerian uses these expressions.

sources.title: 15 Nigerian slang popular among Gen Z
sources.finding: Discusses hardship, everyday joking, style and requests for support in youth slang.
sources.designImplication: Recognise money-related language without initiating money requests or mocking a user's means.

sources.title: What Steeze Really Means
sources.finding: Distinguishes effortless style from adjacent appearance and charm terms.
sources.designImplication: Do not use every fashionable compliment interchangeably or make all characters sound like influencers.

sources.title: 8 Nigerians, 1 Question: Why Did You End a Talking Stage?
sources.finding: Published accounts highlight frustrations around inauthentic presentation, manipulative tests and other early-dating interactions.
sources.designImplication: Write original fictional scenes. Do not copy interviewees' stories, names or private details; this small editorial sample is not population research.

sources.title: Updated Nigerian slang explainer
sources.finding: Shows that some phrases function as teasing, challenge or outright insults depending on the situation.
sources.designImplication: Recognition is broader than generation. Do not reproduce misogynistic labels, sexual shaming or degrading language because an explainer lists them.

sources.title: Nigerian relationship lingos
sources.finding: Explains figurative relationship vocabulary, including heartbreak language.
sources.designImplication: Interpret the surrounding context rather than treating every mention of breakfast as either food or heartbreak.

limitations: Web reporting overrepresents published urban internet culture; it does not replace review by Nigerians across age, gender and regional backgrounds.
The recent sources consulted run through September 2026; no claim is made to capture every new expression as of October 17.
Some sources give different connotations or spellings. Preserve ambiguity and let context lead.
BBC Pidgin and the full State of Love PDF could not be fetched successfully in this session; no findings are attributed to their unread content.
All character dialogue and biographies are original editorial drafts. No real person's messages were collected or used to impersonate them.
